companyIntro.name: Bastion Insurance Group
companyIntro.mission: Price and underwrite risk fairly so claims can always be paid.
companyIntro.culture: Data-led, conservative on assumptions, transparent on exclusions.

projectBackground.name: SME Property Portfolio Review
projectBackground.context: The SME property portfolio's results are slipping. Underwriters must price new business and decide which risks to decline.

manager.name: Greta Lindner
manager.role: Chief Underwriting Officer, Bastion Insurance Group
manager.note: Pricing is a promise to pay claims. If the maths doesn't work, a smile won't.

assignment.title: Price the risk and protect the portfolio
assignment.brief: Calculate ratios and premium, identify adverse selection and moral hazard and write a referral note.

documents.name: New Risk Submission
documents.note: Warehouse sum insured €500,000; expected annual loss 2%.

documents.name: Broker Notes
documents.note: Applicant previously declined by two insurers; sprinklers 'planned'.

tasks.title: Loss Ratio
tasks.prompt: Claims are €600,000 on earned premium of €1,000,000. What is the loss ratio (%)?
tasks.reasoning: The loss ratio shows what share of premium goes on claims.
tasks.mistake: Using written instead of earned premium distorts it.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Combined Ratio
tasks.prompt: With a 60% loss ratio and 35% expense ratio, what is the combined ratio (%)?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Technical Premium
tasks.prompt: Sum insured €500,000 and expected loss 2% gives expected annual loss €10,000. With a 30% load for expenses and profit (x1.3), what premium (€)?
tasks.reasoning: Premium must cover expected loss plus costs and margin.
tasks.mistake: Charging expected loss only guarantees a loss after expenses.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Adverse Selection
tasks.prompt: The applicant was declined by two insurers and now seeks cover from you at a low price. This suggests:
options: Adverse selection — higher-risk applicants seek cover
tasks.reasoning: Risky clients are more likely to seek insurance.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Property Risk Factors
tasks.prompt: Select factors that should affect the price.
tasks.reasoning: Underwriters price hazard, protection and history.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Referral Note
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence underwriting referral note recommending a decision.
tasks.modelAnswer: I recommend declining at the quoted rate and offering terms only once sprinklers are installed and verified. The technical premium is €13,000 but the applicant was declined by two insurers and the broker describes protection as 'planned', which suggests adverse selection. If the client installs sprinklers and provides a certificate, I would quote at €13,000 with a higher excess. Our portfolio combined ratio of 95% leaves little room for under-priced risk.
tasks.reasoning: A good referral gives a decision, the pricing logic and the conditions.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Underpriced Warehouses
caseStudy.background: A portfolio of warehouses was priced on last year's claims, ignoring rising fire risk from unprotected storage. A single fire produced a €4M claim and the combined ratio hit 128%.
caseStudy.solution: Bastion added mandatory risk surveys and protection-based loadings.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Price the hazard, not just the history.
